answer: When controlling for academic resources and test performance (ASVAB composite ability scores and high school class percentile rank), the advantage in college degree completion rates for Black students relative to White students is most pronounced at middle-to-high socioeconomic status (SES) levels. Specifically, Black students exhibit a statistically significant completion advantage in the medium SES stratum (OR = 2.13, p = 0.024) and high SES quartiles (OR ≈ 1.92–1.97), whereas at low SES levels no relative completion advantage is observed (OR = 0.96, p = 0.94).

Synthesized statistical findings into a grounded natural-language hypothesis answering the research question.
